newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares end up on buying of blue-chips.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end up on buying of blue-chips.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index rallied on Monday, largely due to institutional demand for shares of firms with good earnings, brokers said.
Advances in the domestic currency A share market also helped boost sentiment, they said.
The B share index rebounded 1.94 points or 1.23 percent to end at 159.27 on turnover of HK$83.8 million compared with Friday's HK$72.8 million.

The A share index gained 5.47 points or 1.21 percent to 459.09 as speculative buying set in due to an absence of negative news over the weekend, brokers said. Turnover was 8.40 billion yuan on Monday against 9.55 billion on Friday.
The A index fell 1.71 percent last Friday on talk that Beijing was planning measures to cool down the market.
A share turnover was 8.40 billion yuan on Monday against 9.55 billion on Friday. The A index fell 1.71 percent last Friday on talk that Beijing was planning measures to cool down the market.
"Today we see some fresh money flowing into a range of B share firms that have promising prospects," a trader with Shenzhen J & A Securities (H.K.) Ltd said.
"The technical charts of some B stocks look positive after today's rises," the analyst said, adding she expected the B share market to continue to edge up later this week.
But investors are likely to remain cautious in the run-up to April 30, the deadline for listed firms to make public their 1996 annual results, brokers said.
Less than half of the 44 Shenzhen-listed B share firms have released their 1996 annual reports so far.

"I would advise B share investors to wait for more annual reports before buying," an analyst with China Guotai Securities Co said. "I expect the B share index to move between 155-165 points for the rest of this month."
China Merchants Shekou Port Service was the best performer in the B share market, firming HK$0.38 or 7.57 percent to HK$5.40 on volume of 221,860 shares.
Refrigerator maker Hefei Meilin was the most actively traded stock, jumping HK$0.21 to HK$6.36 after 1.13 million shares changed hands.
Meilin's 1996 results showed a strong rise in net profits.

Guangdong Expressway, the biggest loser, slid HK$0.60 or 6.70 percent to HK$8.35 on trade of 1.11 million shares, after the highway operator announced worse-than-expected 1996 results last week, brokers said.
